chunks: And with this chain of narration, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his father, from 'Umar ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Prompt your dead to say: There is no god except Allah, for it erases the sins.' So they asked: 'O Messenger of Allah, what if one says it while healthy?' He replied: 'That is more erasing and more erasing. Indeed, "There is no god except Allah" is a companion to the believer in his life, at his death, and when he is raised.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of reciting 'Laa ilaaha illallah' for the dying and the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* highlights the pivotal role of *Laa ilaaha illallah* as a spiritual safeguard, distinguishing between its efficacy in erasing sins for the dying and its superior, comprehensive comfort for the believer during health, death, and resurrection. Scholarly tradition emphasizes this declaration not merely as a formula for absolution but as a sustaining presence (*uns*) that alleviates the anxiety of the grave and the Day of Judgment, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the continuity of faith from worldly life to the afterlife.
